A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UAVLight and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. All supplied pages were examined. v1 mentions supplementary material but contains none; v2 includes a five-page supplement, whose contents are assessed as newly present in the supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five reconstruction baselines, including PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS results in Tables 4–5 and qualitative comparisons in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations and adds checkpoint-based geometric measurements in Table 6 and supplementary baseline results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The RTK-constrained reconstruction pipeline, frame sampling, filtering, sunlight calculation, and paired lighting-transfer procedure remain substantively unchanged. Newly described ground-control anchoring and checkpoint validation do not establish a revised reconstruction algorithm or baseline model.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 18-scene inventory and outdoor reconstruction/relighting tasks. However, v2's purported remaining-six-scene results include Roof, City2, and City, which lack mappings to that inventory, while Industrial repeats an existing name. The PDFs do not reliably establish whether these are aliases, changed scene coverage, or simply newly reported results for retained coverage.

E2.justification: Both evaluate NeRF-W, NeRF-OSR, GS-W, WildGaussians, and LumiGauss. W-GS and LumiGS in v1 correspond to the expanded names in v2; supplementary GaussianWild corresponds to GS-W. No additional comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 introduces checkpoint-based geometric evaluation across 18 scenes, using approximately 10 checkpoints per scene and vertical/planimetric error measurements. It also revises the reported capture orientation from 'nadir or oblique' to nadir only. The existing A/B evaluation, image metrics, and tabulated training times remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that baseline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4, Table 6, and Figure 4 add a focused analysis checking the metric accuracy of the geometric references against surveyed checkpoints. This addresses reference quality without introducing a broader ablation, sensitivity, or robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions mention fixed random seeds in Section 6.2 without reporting repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new checkpoint averages are geometric-error point estimates, not an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All 180 image-metric entries in v1 Tables 4–5 match v2 Tables 3–4. v2 adds 90 entries in Tables 7–8, new qualitative results, and average vertical/planimetric errors of 10.31/11.83 cm. Grove2's reported area changes from 32,120 to 21,505 square meters. New Table 8 reports Industrial2 PSNR of 24.80 for WildGaussians versus 20.03 for LumiGauss. Ambiguous supplementary scene identities prevent treating these additions as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same RTK-regularized bundle-adjustment objective, grouped reprojection term, sunlight-vector construction, and coordinate transformation. No substantive mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a controlled real-world UAV benchmark, geometric references, and standardized comparison of implicit and explicit illumination methods. The introduction's new accuracy measurements support the existing reference-quality claim without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: The introduction newly explains why image-space and cross-illumination evaluation are particularly suitable for appearance consistency, with geometry providing a metric anchor. Section 4 interprets checkpoint errors as consistent with standard UAV photogrammetry. The main implicit-versus-explicit interpretation and proposed future extensions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplement newly specifies NVIDIA A800 GPUs with 80 GB memory, PyTorch 2.4.1, CUDA 11.8, COLMAP 3.7, and released artifacts; the title page adds a project-page address. Flight altitude and reference anchoring are also newly documented. Conversely, the shortened sunlight description omits some explicit timestamp, coordinate-convention, and alignment explanations from v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds LightCity and positions it as a synthetic urban multi-illumination dataset lacking real-world variability. The broader positioning remains intact. Other bibliography changes mainly update metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Sections 2, 4, and 5 undergo substantial condensation and rewriting, the introduction expands and recasts its contribution bullets, and a supplementary overview and reproducibility section are added. Much of the exposition changes despite retaining the main section sequence. Authorship, affiliations, and baseline terminology also receive edits.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with a checkpoint-validation diagram, additional point clouds, two multi-time galleries, another baseline-comparison figure, and three new tables. Existing tables are relocated, and main qualitative panels are revised, including the Road examples and the Town time label changing from 12:33 to 12:13.

improvement.justification: Table 6 supplies previously missing quantitative validation of geometric-reference accuracy, while the supplement and project address improve reproducibility documentation and access to reported evidence. These are useful gains beyond the unchanged main benchmark scores. However, inconsistent supplementary scene names obstruct verification of the claimed full-scene coverage, and the retained blanket claim of explicit-method superiority is not qualified by the additional counterexamples. The net improvement is therefore limited.
